topics.title: Custom Hooks: Reusing Stateful Logic
topics.summary: A custom hook is a function starting with use that bundles other hooks so logic can be shared between components.
keyPoints: Custom hook = function named useX that calls hooks
Shares logic, not state; every call has its own state
Can accept args and return values or functions
Compose small hooks into bigger ones
Name by purpose (useOnlineStatus), not by mechanism
pitfalls: Believing two components calling the same hook share state.
Naming a function with use but never calling hooks inside (or vice versa).

examples.title: useCounter hook reused twice

interview.a: A function whose name starts with use that calls other hooks, used to share stateful logic between components.

interview.q: Do components that use the same custom hook share state?
interview.a: No. Each call creates its own state; only the logic is shared.

topics.title: useLocalStorage Hook
topics.summary: A hook that behaves like useState but persists the value in localStorage.
keyPoints: Lazy initial state reads from storage once
Write in useEffect when value changes
Wrap parse/set in try/catch
Return [value, setValue] like useState
Do not store sensitive data in localStorage
pitfalls: Reading localStorage during SSR where it does not exist.

examples.title: Persistent notes (survive reload)

interview.q: Why pass a function to useState in useLocalStorage?
interview.a: So localStorage is read only on the first render instead of on every render.

interview.q: What are the risks of localStorage?
interview.a: It is synchronous, string-only, size-limited, can throw in private mode, and is accessible to any script on the origin so it is unsafe for secrets.

topics.title: useFetch Hook
topics.summary: Wrap loading, error, data and cancellation logic in one reusable hook.
keyPoints: Encapsulate data, error, loading in one hook
Cancel with AbortController in cleanup
fetch only rejects on network failure; check response.ok
Ignore AbortError
Production apps should use TanStack Query or SWR
pitfalls: Forgetting to reset loading state when the url changes.
Treating HTTP 404/500 as success because fetch did not throw.

examples.title: useFetch with a simulated async source
examples.explanation: No network is used: a fake fetch function with setTimeout.

interview.a: To cancel in-flight requests when the URL changes or the component unmounts, avoiding stale updates and wasted work.
No. It only rejects on network errors; you must check response.ok or status and throw yourself.

topics.title: useDebounce Hook
topics.summary: Delay reacting to a fast-changing value (like typing) until the user pauses.
keyPoints: Debounce waits for a pause before updating
The effect cleanup cancels the previous timer
Input binds to raw value; work uses debounced value
Throttle limits frequency instead of waiting
Typical delay is 250-500 ms
pitfalls: Debouncing inside the component body without a ref or effect (a new timer each render).
Forgetting to clear the timer, causing updates after unmount.

examples.title: Debounced search term

interview.a: Debounce runs the action only after events stop for a delay; throttle runs it at most once per fixed interval while events continue.

interview.q: How does useDebounce avoid firing on every keystroke?
interview.a: Each change cleans up and restarts a timer, so the debounced value is updated only after the input has been stable for the delay.

topics.title: Utility Hooks: useToggle, usePrevious, useOnClickOutside
topics.summary: A toolbox of tiny hooks you will write again and again: boolean toggles, previous values, outside clicks.
keyPoints: useToggle: boolean state with stable toggle function
usePrevious: store value in a ref inside an effect
useOnClickOutside: document listener + ref.contains
Always remove listeners in cleanup
Consider usehooks-ts or react-use before reinventing
pitfalls: Using click instead of mousedown, causing open-then-close flicker with toggle buttons.

examples.title: Dropdown that closes on outside click

interview.a: It stores the value in a ref inside an effect, so during render the ref still contains the value from the previous render.

interview.q: How do you detect a click outside a component?
interview.a: Attach a document listener and check ref.current.contains(event.target); if false, call the close handler. Clean up the listener on unmount.
